rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal approach with strong encoders (scgpt and imagenet_vit_l) and transformer aggregation, which are promising for capturing complex interactions. It clarifies whether combining RNA and image data improves accuracy. This configuration balances exploration of multimodal processing with reasonable cost, providing foundational insights for subsequent experiments.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieves 0.507 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the transformer aggregation with avgpool, a simpler method that may reduce training cost while maintaining performance. It clarifies whether aggregation complexity impacts accuracy, balancing exploration of architectural choices with cost efficiency.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scgpt and imagenet_vit_l encoders (config_009) achieve 0.5176 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing concat fusion with weighted fusion in the same architecture to potentially improve accuracy. The change targets a key design choice (fusion method) with minimal cost increase (estimated ~7.18 GPU hours), balancing exploitation of promising components and exploration of hyperparameter sensitivity.

The existing evidence shows config_016 (avgpool+weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.542). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with weighted fusion using the same RNA/image encoders, which could reveal if transformer aggregation improves accuracy. It balances exploitation (building on successful components) and exploration (testing a different aggregation method). Expected cost: ~3.95 GPU hours (similar to config_001), keeping total cost low while testing a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows config_016 (avgpool+weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.5419). This experiment tests using transformer aggregation with weighted fusion while switching to resnet50 image encoder (smaller model) and keeping scgpt RNA encoder. This balances exploration of aggregation methods and exploitation of the current best RNA/image encoder combination, with expected similar cost to config_016.

Existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion (config_016) achieves the highest accuracy (0.542) at low cost (2.94 GPU hours). This experiment tests using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which could improve performance by leveraging a different RNA encoder and more robust image features. It balances exploration of RNA/image encoder combinations with similar aggregation/fusion methods to the current best, while keeping cost comparable to previous experiments.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and weighted fusion (e.g., config_017) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using imagenet_vit_l (a larger image encoder) instead of resnet50 (used in config_017) improves performance while maintaining transformer aggregation. It clarifies the impact of image encoder choice on accuracy, a critical design choice. The expected cost is similar to config_009 (7.18 GPU hours), balancing exploration of image encoder efficacy with budget constraints.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_013) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests the impact of changing the fusion method to concat while keeping other parameters the same, which could clarify if the fusion method significantly affects performance. It is the best use of the remaining budget as it explores a critical design choice with a similar cost to the current top performer.

The existing evidence shows that models using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_013) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests a logical extension by using scvi_n200 with resnet50 image encoder and concat fusion, which could improve performance while keeping costs manageable. It balances exploration of image encoder variations and exploitation of the scvi_n200 RNA encoder's strength, with an expected cost similar to config_017 (6.22 GPU hours).

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and weighted fusion (e.g., config_013, 0.724989 accuracy) perform best. This experiment tests aggregation=None with concat fusion, a variation that could improve accuracy by simplifying interactions. It is the final experiment and balances exploration of aggregation methods with cost efficiency (estimated lower cost than transformer aggregation).
